NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's web site under City Council Meeting agendas at www.RollingHillsEstates.gov and
  during regular business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's web
  site and a recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP -TV
  Channel 35 (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome on any item during City Council consideration of the item. An opportunity is
  also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If you would like to
  address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public comment, please
  complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  OCTOBER 28, 2025

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR STEGURA called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by MAYOR STEGURA.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura

City Council Members Absent:  Zerunyan

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Donald M. Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Development/Public Works Director Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson
  Public Works Manager Kirsten Graham

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING NOVEMBER AS NATIVE AMERICAN HERITAGE
  MONTH

MAYOR STEGURA declared November as Native American Heritage Month.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-G AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF SEPTEMBER & OCTOBER 2025

  APPROVED WARRANTS 68989 THROUGH 69052 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $493,836.22 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 100425 THROUGH
  100525; IN THE AMOUNT OF $103,595.21; FOR A GRAND TOTAL
  AMOUNT OF $597,431.43 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF SEPTEMBER 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF SEPTEMBER 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
OCTOBER 28, 2025
 E.  TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 17, 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 14, 2025

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

G.  COMMISSION/COMMITTEE ATTENDANCE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

None.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  INTRODUCTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 758 AMENDING AND RESTATING
  MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 3.32 - PROCUREMENT OF EQUIPMENT, GOODS,
  AND SERVICES

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Introduce for a first reading, Ordinance
  No. 757; and 2) Direct staff to bring back Ordinance No. 758 for a second reading
  and adoption at the City Council meeting of November 18, 2025.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  INTRODUCE FOR A FIRST READING, ORDINANCE NO. 758; AND DIRECT
  STAFF TO BRING BACK ORDINANCE NO. 758 FOR A SECOND READING
  AND ADOPTION AT THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING OF NOVEMBER 18,
  2025.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 758 by title.

B.  TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: INTRODUCTION OF ORDINANCE
  NO. 756 AMENDING AND RESTATING MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 10.12 AND
  ORDINANCE NO. 757 ADOPTING SPEED LIMITS IN SPECIAL SPEED ZONES

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Introduce for a first reading, Ordinance
  No. 756 and Ordinance No. 757; 2) Direct staff to bring back Ordinance No. 756 and
  Ordinance No. 757 for a second reading and adoption at the City Council meeting of
  November 18, 2025; and 3) Provide direction regarding any additional signage or
  supplemental visibility measures.

Public Works Manager Graham provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER summarized that there was consensus of the Traffic &
Safety Committee for the speed limit signs to be highlighted in each of the three locations where
the speed limit will change.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 28, 2025
 Community Development and Public Works Director Naughton summarized the enhanced
sign options as outlined on the map in the staff report.

Public Works Manager Graham confirmed the tree trimming cost would be separate, and
included in the regular maintenance contract, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

Public Works Manager Graham confirmed AB 43 was passed in 2021, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

MAYOR STEGURA proposed deferring the type of signage to the Committee and staff.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  INTRODUCE FOR A FIRST READING, ORDINANCE NO. 756; AND DIRECT
  STAFF TO BRING BACK ORDINANCE NO. 756 FOR SECOND READING
  AND ADOPTION AT THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING OF NOVEMBER 18,
  2025.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance 756 by title.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  INTRODUCE FOR A FIRST READING, ORDINANCE NO. 757; AND DIRECT
  STAFF TO BRING BACK ORDINANCE NO. 757 FOR SECOND READING
  AND ADOPTION AT THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING OF NOVEMBER 18,
  2025.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance 757 by title.

C.  APPROVAL OF A MASTER AGREEMENT AUTHORIZING AFFORDABLE HOUSING
  AND IMPOSING AFFORDABLE HOUSING RESALE RESTRICTIONS ON REAL
  PROPERTY WITH RHE-75, LLC, FOR THE LA SEVILLA PROJECT LOCATED AT
  927 DEEP VALLEY DRIVE, AND DIRECTING STAFF TO UTILIZE THE FORM OF
  AGREEMENT FOR FUTURE PROJECTS REQUIRED TO PROVIDE FOR-SALE
  AFFORDABLE UNITS

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Approve the Proposed Affordable
  Housing Agreement with RHE-75, LLC; and 2) Direct staff to use the Proposed
  Affordable Housing Agreement as a template for future projects that have a for-sale
  affordable housing requirement.

Community Development and Public Works Director Naughton provided a staff report (as
per the agenda material).

Scott Anastasi, representative of the developer and ownership of the property, explained the
process for prequalifying and selecting interested parties for the units, confirming there will not
be a lottery for the units, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

Mr. Anastasi summarized the amenities available at the property, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER HUFF.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 28, 2025
 Mr. Anastasi stated that the property is currently insured, and that the individual homeowners
will get policies for their interior units, in response to MAYOR STEGURA’s concern the project
being insurable given its location near a high severity fire zone.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE PROPOSED AFFORDABLE HOUSING AGREEMENT WITH
  RHE-75, LLC; AND DIRECT STAFF TO USE THE PROPOSED AFFORDABLE
  HOUSING AGREEMENT AS A TEMPLATE FOR FUTURE PROJECTS THAT
  HAVE A FOR-SALE AFFORDABLE HOUSING REQUIREMENT.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 755 ESTABLISHING A PERMIT PROCEDURE
  AND REGULATIONS FOR COMMERCIAL AND STUDENT FILMING; AND
  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 2611 ESTABLISHING PERMIT FEES FOR
  COMMERCIAL AND STUDENT FILM PERMITS

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Review and provide any direction to the
  City Manager and Community Development Director on the proposed film permit
  Rules and Regulations; 2) Hold a second reading and adopt Ordinance No. 755; and
  3) Adopt Resolution No. 2611 updating the Community Development Department and
  Public Works Fee Schedule with respect to permit fees for commercial and student
  film permits.

Community Development and Public Works Director Naughton provided a staff report (as
per the agenda material).

Director Naughton explained that the City’s commercial filming and photography rules and
regulations can be found on the City’s website and on the City’s application form, in response
to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER.

Director Naughton explained that applications are routed to the Sherriff’s and Fire
Department directly, in response to MAYOR STEGURA.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 755.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 755 by title.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2611.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 28, 2025
 City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2611 by title.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended the California Association of Councils of Governments
(CALCOG) Housing Law and Policy Update in Sacramento on October 27.

MAYOR STEGURA attended the South Bay Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG) Board
meeting on October 23, and plans to attend the Clean Power Alliance Board meeting on
November 6.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  AUTHORIZATION TO ATTEND THE CALIFORNIA CONTRACT CITIES
  ASSOCIATION'S ANNUAL SACRAMENTO LEGISLATIVE TOUR, JANUARY 5 - 7,
  2026

  CONSENSUS ANY/ALL COUNCIL MEMBERS MAY ATTEND.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF congratulated City staff on the well-attended Prepared Peninsula
Expo on October 26.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL-ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Initiation of litigation pursuant to Government Code section 54956.9(d)(4)
  One potential case

  AUTHORIZED STAFF TO SUPPORT THE CITY OF REDONDO BEACH IN
  THE LITIGATION CONCERNING ITS HOUSING ELEMENT BY JOINING IN
  AN AMICUS BRIEF SEEKING CALIFORNIA SUPREME COURT REVIEW AND
  ANY OTHER EFFORTS TO LIMIT THE SCOPE OF THE APPELLATE COURT
  DECISION.

B.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATORS
  Government Code section 54956.8 Property: 927 Deep Valley Drive
  Agency negotiator: City Manager, Community Development Director, City Attorney
  Negotiating parties: RHE-75, LLC
  Under negotiation: price and terms of payment

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:04 p.m. MAYOR STEGURA adjourned the meeting in memory of Lead Maintenance
Worker Francisco Sosa. The meeting was adjourned to Tuesday, November 18, 2025 at
7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a regular meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Debby Stegura, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
OCTOBER 28, 2025
